full_text_en:
Liaoning Securities Company et al. (Five Financial Enterprises) v. Liaoning Light Industry Supply and Marketing Company and Shenyang Oil and Chemical Plant — dispute over financing bonds

Plaintiff: Liaoning Securities Company.
Legal representative: Shao Rongdi, General Manager.
Agent ad litem: Li Huanmin, employee of the Company.

Plaintiff: China Agricultural Bank Liaoning Trust and Investment Company.
Legal representative: Wu Hongbin, Deputy General Manager (presiding).
Agent ad litem: Dong Yingxin, employee of the Company.

Plaintiff: China Industrial and Commercial Bank Liaoning Joint-Stock Trust and Investment Company.
Legal representative: Gao Shengyan, General Manager.
Agent ad litem: Zhang Chengwu, employee of the Company.

Plaintiff: Liaoning International Trust and Investment Company.
Legal representative: Wang Yongduo, General Manager.
Agent ad litem: Liu Yan, Legal Counsel of the Company.
Agent ad litem: Li Jie, employee of the Company.

Plaintiff: Liaoning Trust and Investment Company.
Legal representative: Wu Shirong, General Manager.
Agent ad litem: Wan Muyuan and Yang Jinming, employees of the Company.

Defendant: Liaoning Light Industry Supply and Marketing Company.
Legal representative: Xie Zhenyang, General Manager.
Agent ad litem: Xu Chunxian, employee of the Company.
Agent ad litem: Lin Jiang, lawyer of Shenyang No. 1 Cooperative Law Firm.

Defendant: Shenyang Oil and Chemical Plant.
Legal representative: Jia Jitai, Plant Manager.
Agent ad litem: Liu Wenlu and Li Fengru, cadres of the Plant.

The plaintiffs Liaoning Securities Company, China Agricultural Bank Liaoning Trust and Investment Company, China Industrial and Commercial Bank Liaoning Joint-Stock Trust and Investment Company, Liaoning International Trust and Investment Company, and Liaoning Trust and Investment Company (hereinafter referred to as the five plaintiffs) filed a lawsuit with the Liaoning High People's Court against the defendants Liaoning Light Industry Supply and Marketing Company (hereinafter referred to as the Supply and Marketing Company) and Shenyang Oil and Chemical Plant (hereinafter referred to as the Chemical Plant) regarding a dispute over financing bonds.

The five plaintiffs alleged that on May 30, 1992, they jointly issued corporate bonds in the amount of RMB 60 million for the defendant Supply and Marketing Company, with a term of one year and an annual interest rate of 9.072%. The defendant Chemical Plant provided a guarantee. Upon expiration of the contract, the Supply and Marketing Company only paid the five plaintiffs RMB 2.7 million in interest. Therefore, they requested that the court order the defendants to repay the matured principal and interest totaling RMB 63,343,200 and assume liability for breach of contract.

The defendant Supply and Marketing Company argued that the main reason for its default in repaying the principal and interest was that the five plaintiffs failed to extend the issuance as approved by the Liaoning Branch of the People's Bank of China, and thus bore responsibility for the dispute. It requested an extension for repayment.

The defendant Chemical Plant argued that the issuance of RMB 60 million in bonds by the Supply and Marketing Company was erroneous and violated legal provisions, rendering the guarantee invalid, and therefore it should not bear the liability of guarantee.

The Liaoning High People's Court found through trial that on May 23, 1992, upon approval by the Liaoning Branch of the People's Bank of China via Document No. 14 (1992) LiaoYinJinZi, the defendant Supply and Marketing Company issued financing bonds of RMB 60 million to the public, with an annual interest rate of 9.027% and a term of one year, from May 30, 1992 to May 30, 1993. Among these, Liaoning Securities Company underwrote RMB 20 million, and each of the other plaintiffs underwrote RMB 10 million. The underwriting contracts were all guaranteed by the Chemical Plant. After the contracts were signed, the five plaintiffs timely transferred the full amount of RMB 60 million to the account designated by the Supply and Marketing Company and sold the financing bonds externally. Upon expiration of the contracts, the Supply and Marketing Company failed to redeem all of the principal, paying only RMB 2.7 million in interest, of which RMB 600,000 was paid to Liaoning Securities Company, RMB 900,000 to China Agricultural Bank Liaoning Trust and Investment Company, RMB 300,000 to China Industrial and Commercial Bank Liaoning Joint-Stock Trust and Investment Company, RMB 450,000 to Liaoning International Trust and Investment Company, and RMB 450,000 to Liaoning Trust and Investment Company. The outstanding principal and interest owed to the five plaintiffs were respectively: RMB 21,214,400 to Liaoning Securities Company, RMB 10,007,200 to China Agricultural Bank Liaoning Trust and Investment Company, RMB 10,607,200 to China Industrial and Commercial Bank Liaoning Joint-Stock Trust and Investment Company, RMB 10,457,200 to Liaoning International Trust and Investment Company, and RMB 10,457,200 to Liaoning Trust and Investment Company.

The Liaoning High People's Court held that the financing bond agreements respectively signed between the defendant Supply and Marketing Company and the five plaintiffs, having been approved by the Liaoning Branch of the People's Bank of China, were lawful and valid pursuant to Article 4 of the Provisional Regulations on the Administration of Enterprise Bonds promulgated by the State Council. The Supply and Marketing Company's failure to repay the entire matured principal and interest in accordance with the agreements violated Article 8 of the aforesaid Regulations, which provides that "bondholders have the right to receive interest and recover the principal on schedule." In accordance with Article 112, paragraph 2, of the General Principles of the Civil Law of the People's Republic of China, the Supply and Marketing Company shall bear liability for breach of contract and, as agreed in the agreements, pay an additional penalty of 50% on the original interest rate. As to the Supply and Marketing Company's argument that it failed to repay the principal and interest of the bonds because the plaintiffs did not extend the issuance, since extension of bond issuance is not a necessary condition for debt repayment and no such stipulation existed in the original agreements, the Supply and Marketing Company's defense could not be sustained. The defendant Chemical Plant, as an independent enterprise legal person, had a clear expression of intention in its guarantee contract; the guarantee was lawful and valid, and it shall bear joint and several liability. Accordingly, the Liaoning High People's Court rendered judgment on September 6, 1993:

1. The defendant Liaoning Light Industry Supply and Marketing Company shall, within one month from the effective date of this judgment, repay to the plaintiff Liaoning Securities Company RMB 21,214,400, to the plaintiff China Agricultural Bank Liaoning Trust and Investment Company RMB 10,007,200, to the plaintiff China Industrial and Commercial Bank Liaoning Joint-Stock Trust and Investment Company RMB 10,607,200, to the plaintiff Liaoning Trust and Investment Company RMB 10,457,200, and to the plaintiff Liaoning International Trust and Investment Company RMB 10,457,200, and shall bear interest for overdue payment at an annual rate of 12.608%, calculated from May 31, 1993 until the date of full repayment.

2. The defendant Shenyang Oil and Chemical Plant shall bear joint and several liability for the aforesaid sums payable by the defendant Liaoning Light Industry Supply and Marketing Company in the event that the latter fails to perform.

Court acceptance fee and property preservation fee: RMB 637,994, to be borne by the defendant Liaoning Light Industry Supply and Marketing Company.

After the judgment of first instance, both the plaintiffs and the defendants accepted the judgment and did not file an appeal.
